credits_cram.why: "CRAM is the method of \citet{hoover2026cram}, not ours." It is also described as a re-implementation. The authors' names are not spelled out, but it is clearly credited as an existing method.

cites_hoover.why: The body text uses \citep{hoover2026cram} and \citet{hoover2026cram} in the abstract, introduction, related work and analysis.

small_n.why: "the direct-solving arm uses only 5--10 puzzles per model for cost reasons"; the paper says its estimates are very uncertain.

handset_caveat.why: "The one-weight energy solved 497/500 puzzles, equal to the best learned seed and within one puzzle of the others", matching the original authors' caution.

their_numbers.why: "The original paper reports 42 ms on an H200 GPU; this is their number and we did not measure it." The 99.996% figure is likewise attributed to the original paper.

no_new_claims.why: Every experiment and number traces to the log. Wilson intervals, the rule-of-three bound and the cost extrapolations are derived from logged counts and are labeled as such.
